title: Selection miss learns, flaky is muted
desiredOutcome: A full run that fails on a suite no derived sign-off gate listed prints SELECTION MISS and records it, and full-gate.py files a bug and a coupling for it only when the runner named that suite as failing; a muted suite's failure is recorded but neither blocks a verdict nor teaches a coupling, an expired mute blocks again, and Playwright's flaky tests are recorded as flaky beside a passing verdict rather than as passes or failures.

tasks.title: meta.muted and coupling.lastCaught: schema, vocabulary, validator
tasks.description: Schema: meta.muted (array of {test path, reason, owner, until ISO date, bugId}; absent means nothing is quarantined and every failure blocks) and meta.coupling[].lastCaught (the ts of the newest third-place run that named the coupled test as failing; absent means never caught since it was learned). KNOWN_META += muted. Validator: a muted entry whose bugId is missing, or names no bug in bugs[], is a FINDING - a mute with no bug is the retry-until-green shape this exists to refuse, and it is wrong from the moment it is written. An EXPIRED until is a WARNING naming the entry and the unmute or extend command - NOT a finding, and this deviates from the lane on purpose: every mutating verb pre-validates and refuses a manifest already carrying a finding (_locked_retarget: 'the manifest is already invalid -- nothing written'), and DEFAULT_GATE holds invalid, so a date-triggered finding would freeze every verb and fail every default CI gate on the expiry day, including the verb that lifts the mute. The runner's refusal to honour an expired mute (L4.c) is the enforcement. Reverting to a finding is a one-word change plus exempting the mute verbs from their own pre-check, the repair-tests-add precedent. A duplicate test, a missing owner or reason, and an unparseable until are warnings. SCHEMA_EXEMPTIONS rows for the new fields, with the reason. Red-first: a muted entry without bugId is a finding; one naming a bug id bugs[] does not hold is a finding (mutation: accept any string -> red); an expired until is a warning and the manifest stays valid (mutation: make it a finding -> red). Allow case: a well-formed unexpired entry validates clean.

add: plugins/audit/tests/test_validate_manifest.py: repro that FAILS on current code - a meta.muted entry with no bugId, or one naming a bug the plan does not hold, validates with no finding

outcome.technical: _manifest_vocab gains mute_until, mute_expired and mute_today (the UTC day, which the runner will import so both read one clock); _manifest_rules._check_muted emits the findings and warnings; the demo exempts meta.muted with a reason.
outcome.descriptive: meta.muted and coupling.lastCaught are in the schema and the vocabulary; a mute without a bug, or naming a bug the plan lacks, is a validator finding; an expired until is a warning that names the unmute and extend commands

tasks.title: bug-add writes the bug shape /audit:bug spells; mute and unmute write meta.muted
tasks.description: audit-task.py bug-add "<title>" [manifest] --severity low|med|high --description TEXT --files a,b [--repro TEXT] [--expected TEXT] [--actual TEXT] writes exactly the shape commands/bug.md step 3 spells - {id, title, status 'open', severity, reportedAt, reportedBy null, description, repro, expected, actual, files, taskId null, fixedIn null, notes null} - with the id from _id_shape.next_bug_id(assembled, suffix) (the allocator next-id bug already uses, suffix from _mint_suffix), creating bugs [] when absent, under _under_lock, into the index through _write_add(..., phase_id=None, index_fields=('bugs',)) (the index-only path P69 added), revalidated with roll-back, journal row bug.add. The title is the POSITIONAL, not a --title flag: this parser's positional slot is named title, and the --rename comment in build_parser records why a --title flag would shadow it. --repro, --expected and --actual join PROSE_FLAGS. mute --test <path> --reason TEXT --owner NAME --until <date> --bug <id> and unmute --test <path> are the only writers of meta.muted (same lock, index write with index_fields=('meta',), revalidation, journal test.muted / test.unmuted); mute on an already-muted test with a later until extends it. Because an expired mute is a warning (L4.a), unmute and an extending mute run on such a plan like every other verb. commands/bug.md steps 1-3 become the bug-add call (no hand edit of bugs[]) and /audit:bug add passes its gathered answers as flags; the /audit:bug README row and commands/task.md for mute and unmute (_refs.command_flag_drift). Red-first: bug-add writes the step-3 shape with every key present, an allocator id and one journal row; on a plan with no bugs key it creates the list; mute without --bug refused; mute naming a bug the plan lacks is refused by the validator's finding and rolled back (mutation: skip the revalidation -> red). Allow case: unmute of a muted test removes exactly that entry.

tasks.title: A muted suite's failure is recorded and does not block; Playwright's flaky is its own word
tasks.description: Verdict rule (dg20): a failed step whose failingSuites (named basis only) are ALL muted by an unexpired meta.muted entry does not make the run fail - failed_steps / run_status exclude it - and the step keeps its exit, failing and failingSuites on the row; the row gets muted [{test, bugId, until}] and the terminal prints 'muted: <test> failed (bug <bugId>, until <date>)'. A step with one non-muted failing suite, or whose failures could not be named (tail basis), fails as today: a mute is never assumed. An expired entry is not honoured, and the line says 'muted until <date> - expired, so this failure blocks'. The runner never retries a non-muted failure (a retry stays reserved for a signal death). Playwright: add a summary reader row (passed, failed and flaky counted as ran) and a failure reader row TOGETHER (fr0 reads _SUMMARY_READERS and _FAILURE_READERS against each other), and a step observation flaky (the names Playwright reports as flaky) with flakyBasis, recorded on a step that exited 0 as well. NOT a step outcome: _evidence_io._step_failed and every tally read any outcome as not-passed, and a flaky-but-green step is a pass with a named doubt. Capture a real Playwright run's list or line reporter output as the fixture before writing the regex (the verifying-external-behavior skill): the reader must match what the pinned version prints. _evidence_io: muted on the row (row_for allow-list), flaky and flakyBasis in STEP_KEYS, bounded and redacted. Red-first: dg20 - a muted failing suite beside green steps -> status passed with the muted line (mutation: remove the filter -> red); allow: an expired until -> the failure blocks (mutation: ignore until -> red); a muted suite beside an unmuted failure -> failed; a tail-basis failure -> failed. Playwright output with one flaky test -> step exit 0, flaky names it, status passed (mutation: record it as outcome -> red, through gate_tally counting it failed).

add: plugins/audit/tests/test_run_test_gate.py: repro that FAILS on current code - a run whose only failing suite is muted by an unexpired entry comes back failed (dg20)
plugins/audit/tests/test_run_test_gate.py: repro that FAILS on current code - Playwright output reporting a flaky test records nothing that names it

outcome.technical: diverges from the description by tightening it after three reviews: the description's rule (all failingSuites muted, named basis) let a second failure through in wrappers, package scripts, multi-runner steps and several runner shapes, so the rule fails closed (mute_ineligible, command_runner, MUTE_RUNNERS) over real captures of pytest 9.1.1, jest 30.5.2, vitest 4.1.10 and Playwright 1.56.0; a step-level muted marker is on the committed row, and the tallies, the shadow claim, derive-phase-gate and audit-lookup read it. Known limit, stated in MUTE_RUNNERS: a jest reporter error prints nothing, so a mute beside it holds.
outcome.descriptive: a mute is honoured only for a direct call of an allow-listed runner (pytest, jest, vitest, Playwright) that exits with its failed-tests code, whose named failures match its tally and which reports no other failure state; anything else keeps the gate red; Playwright's flaky tests are named on a step without being an outcome

tasks.title: The --full post-pass names a SELECTION MISS, learning only from a suite the runner named
tasks.description: After a --full run, a post-pass (dg15). Failing suites = the steps' failingSuites whose basis says the runner NAMED them - never the failing tail, never a muted suite. Derived sets = the union of phase.testGateDerived.tests over the phases whose mergedHead the run's head contains (_worktrees.merged_into) and that merged after the newest earlier whole-bearing green full row. A failing suite none of them listed is a SELECTION MISS: print 'SELECTION MISS: <path> failed at the third place and no derived sign-off gate in <P, ...> listed it. remedy: audit-task.py couple --test <path> --sources <files> --basis-run <runId> --basis-head <head> --phases <ids>; audit-task.py bug-add ...' and put selectionMiss [{test, phases, sources}] on the row (row_for allow-list). Sources are the union of those phases' tasks' files - the work since the last green full run, read off the plan rather than guessed from a diff. When the failures were not named, print 'not learned: the runner did not name the failing suites (basis: <basis>)' instead. The runner prints and records; it never writes the manifest - full-gate.py acts. Red-first: a full run failing on e2e/cart.spec.ts, with one merged phase whose derived tests do not list it, prints the miss and records it; dg15 - the same failure with a tail basis records no miss and prints the not-learned line (mutation: learn from the tail -> red). Allow cases: a failing suite a derived gate listed is not a miss; a muted suite is never a miss.

One reading of named failing suites (_evidence_io.named_failing_suites) now serves run-test-gate, the shadow claim and derive-phase-gate; newest_whole_bearing is its single home. Also fixed at its source: a step's named paths were a set, which crashed every --json dump.

tasks.title: couple --caught refreshes a coupling's lastCaught from a named third-place failure
tasks.description: couple --test <path> --caught <runId> on an already-coupled test sets lastCaught to that run's ts and journals coupling.caught. The run must be a scope full row whose failingSuites, with a named basis, include the test (looked up with _evidence_io.row_by_run); otherwise refused exit 2 naming which. A coupling first written from a miss carries no lastCaught. --caught never creates a coupling (a test that is not coupled is refused) and never changes sources. Add the dest to VERB_FLAGS['couple'] and commands/task.md. Red-first: --caught on a coupled test named failing in a full row sets lastCaught to the row's ts and writes one journal row; mutation: accept a row whose basis is a tail -> red. Allow cases: an uncoupled test refused; a phase-scope row refused. Also, in the same file: audit-task's `_named_failing_suites` (the reader behind a fix task's --failing-from gate) must skip a step the committed row marks muted (the step-level `muted` marker P81.3 adds to STEP_KEYS), so a quarantined suite never narrows a fix task's gate; correct its docstring that says it reads a failed step the way run-test-gate.failed_steps does. Red-first: a failed row whose only failing suite is a muted step yields no failing-from paths.

tasks.title: The doctor names untracked couplings and uncouple candidates, never removing either
tasks.description: check_couplings(rep, project, manifest_rel, manifest, git_root, config=None) in _doctor_trail.py, wired after the full-run row. (dg5) A coupling whose test or any source git does not track (one batched git ls-files over the named paths) is a WARNING naming the path and 'audit-task.py uncouple --test <path>' - never removed silently. A coupling not caught (lastCaught, else learnedAt) in the last K green whole-bearing full runs is named as a CANDIDATE for uncouple, with K printed as the basis (a module constant with its reason); never removed, because removal narrows the gate. No meta.coupling: an OK row. Red-first: delete the coupled test file in a fixture repo -> the doctor names it with the command (mutation: skip untracked paths -> red). Allow cases: a coupling caught recently is not a candidate; one older than K green full runs is.

tasks.title: full-gate.py acts on a miss: a coupling and a bug, and nothing from an unnamed failure
tasks.description: After the --full --record subprocess, full-gate.py reads the row it wrote (_evidence_io.row_by_run with the runId the runner printed on its 'evidence: recorded' line; failing that, the newest full row for HEAD) and, for each selectionMiss entry, runs audit-task.py couple --test <path> --sources <sources> --basis-run <runId> --basis-head <head> --phases <ids>, then audit-task.py bug-add "Selection miss: <path>" --severity med --files <path> --description <the miss sentence, the runId, the head and the phases>, both as subprocesses through _loader.script_path; and couple --test <t> --caught <runId> for each already-coupled test named failing. It prints what it wrote and each verb's own output, and exits with the runner's code: a miss is learned and the red still blocks the push. It never acts on a row whose failures were not named. Red-first in test_full_gate.py: a fake full run producing a miss ends with a coupling and a bug in the fixture plan and one journal row each; dg15 end to end - a tail-basis red writes nothing (mutation: act on the failing lines -> red). Allow case: a green run writes nothing.

Guide fence, tree line and full-gate section; _deps.py comment.

tasks.title: Docs: the learning loop, quarantine and flaky
tasks.description: reference/orchestrator.md: the learning loop - a miss at the third place becomes a coupling and a bug through full-gate.py, only from a suite the runner named; removal is uncouple by a person, never automatic. Quarantine: a muted suite is run and recorded, never blocks, never teaches, and blocks again when its until passes; no retry-until-green. reference/manifest-conventions.md: the bug.add, test.muted, test.unmuted and coupling.caught journal actions and their details. commands/doctor.md: the coupling row. commands/review.md: what --full now learns. README: meta.muted and a flaky step, and what a SELECTION MISS asks of the operator. COMPATIBILITY.md: muted absent = nothing quarantined; lastCaught absent = never caught since learned; an expired mute is a warning and why it is not a finding. CHANGELOG.md [Unreleased]. No numbers in prose, no register ids.

tasks.title: status tests read only the locks their own fixture holds
tasks.description: Fault F520. test_audit_status.py cv2 and sh0 compare the CLI's bare output with a hand-built render_status() call; run directly inside a checkout that holds a live phase-<id> lock (.git/audit-locks, shared by every worktree of the clone), the CLI side prints an unfinished-work block naming that real lock, so both fail - the isolated sweep hides it. Point the lock lookup at the fixture's own git directory (or inject it through a seam audit-status already has), so a real lock elsewhere cannot reach the render. Red-first: run the two cases while a real lock is held and see them fail before the fix. Allow: a lock planted in the fixture's own git directory is still rendered.

tasks.title: the evidence ledger's readers decode through one function, and a byte that does not decode is a finding everywhere
tasks.description: Fault F523. read_rows opens ledger files with errors='replace' and reports them fully read, while verify opens them strictly and grades them unreadable; every consumer of read_rows (status, doctor, panel, report, the release guard's full-run answer, import-evidence) can compare a value a replaced byte silently changed. Both readers (and any sibling that opens a ledger file) decode through ONE function; a non-UTF-8 byte is a finding on every surface - read_rows counts the file as lost (unreadableFiles), never returns its rows as clean. Red-first as above; allow: a clean UTF-8 file with non-ASCII text reads as before.

add: plugins/audit/tests/test__evidence_io.py: one invalid byte planted inside a runId - read_rows and verify grade that file the same (unreadable), and no row with a replaced character is returned as clean

outcome.technical: _evidence_io: ledger_decode/ledger_text (strict) serve read_rows, verify, append_row (refuses an undecodable target), import-evidence and the audit-journal evidence merge (refuses an undecodable side); stamp_moment (parse_ts plus ISO date) feeds oldest_first/newest_row, which row_by_run, latest_by_subject, reusable_run, gate_last_caught, earliest_recorded, boundary_of and a derived _newest_first all use; boundary_of hands at on in the Z spelling and names every unplaceable or missing stamp in unknown; _verdict_binding blocks on an unplaceable subject row, words a lost file apart, and finds a reused origin by row_by_run; the panel reads newest per runId through the same order. Recorded elsewhere: the other text-ordered readers and _epoch (F530), run-test-gate --record exiting 0 unrecorded (F532).
outcome.descriptive: Every reader and writer of the evidence ledger decodes a file one strict way and orders rows by the moment a stamp names; a byte that is not UTF-8, or a stamp that places no moment, is named or refused on every surface instead of being silently repaired or dropped.

intentCheck.basis: the description asked for one decode across the ledger's readers; review widened the task to the ledger's moment order, the evidence boundary, the merge verb and the panel, each because this task's change made a claim there false or left the same question answered two ways

tasks.title: a full-scope row that names no tested head cannot bear whole

Add 'the row names no tested head' as a disqualification reason so the walk skips it and a basis names it. Allow: rows with a head are unaffected.

tasks.title: the status gate can fail on a merged phase whose full-run answer is unknown
tasks.description: Fault F527. provisional_phases and stale_full_runs count PROVISIONAL rows only and no condition in _status_facts.CONDITIONS names UNKNOWN, so '--gate --fail-on provisional,stale-full-run' is green over a plan whose third place cannot be answered at all (no mergedHead, git could not answer, or an unreadable ledger), while this repository's release guard refuses over the same phase. Add a new OPT-IN condition 'unknown-full-run' (additive, outside DEFAULT_GATE like its siblings) that names each such phase with full_status's basis; do not change what 'provisional' covers. commands/status.md lists it with the others. tasks.title: add --failing-from resolves a runner-named suite to one repository path
tasks.description: A fix task created with add --failing-from puts the runner's spelling of each named failing suite straight into its gate, and run-test-gate runs that gate from the project root. A suite the runner named relative to its own directory (test_old.py for backend/tests/test_old.py) becomes a path that does not exist, so the fix task's gate cannot run (probed: python3 test_old.py exits 2, can't open file). Resolve each named suite before _union_paths: keep it when it exists from the project root; otherwise take the single tracked file (git ls-files) it matches by the listed_by suffix rule; when none or several match, fall through to the ordinary task gate and say why first, the way the tail-basis case does. Reuse the one resolver the catch rule uses (a runner spelling resolves to exactly one candidate, or names why not) rather than a second matcher. Red-first: an ff case where a runner-relative spelling must come out as the repository-root path, one where two tracked files share the suffix (falls through with the reason), and one where the spelling already exists from the root (kept as written).
